title: Restore editorial context handler data-client configuration
description:
Fresh read-only verification on the intended TI app in papyrus-production found getEditorialContext fails at publication scope and both selected sections. Deployed assignment handler throws Lambda:Unhandled: The data environment variables are malformed. Expected string values for: _MODEL_INTROSPECTION_SCHEMA_BUCKET_NAME, _MODEL_INTROSPECTION_SCHEMA_KEY, _GRAPHQL_ENDPOINT. Canonical publication, current private doctrine metadata and section identifiers can be read through the same API; no policy bodies are recorded here. This is independent of the two proposed private query reads on the editorial-checks role. Source assignment handler calls getAmplifyDataClientConfig, while root schema resource authorization currently omits assignmentAction; root cause and least-privilege configuration correction need a reviewed source fix and synthetic/deployed acceptance. Do not add broad allow.resource access as an unreviewed shortcut. Active PR367 data/backend patches were checked and do not fix this handler configuration. Migration records and soft claims checked eligible/unassigned; no migration operation is claimed. Codex owns the source correction on draft PR382. SDK registration, offline configuration coverage and field-scoped synthesis are implemented. Review/CI, exact consumer synthesis, access approval, release and zero-provider deployed acceptance remain pending. No deployment or live access change has occurred.

Feature: Resolve private editorial context on the deployed consumer
Scenario: Read current context without a model call
Given the configured consumer publication and permitted authenticated actor
When current publication and selected-section editorial context is requested
Then the existing handler initializes its supported data client and returns validated scoped context and source revisions
And credentials, other-tenant records and private policy text are absent from public errors
And zero provider requests or policy mutations occur.

Keep rollout blocked until the source fix, exact permission/configuration diff and zero-provider runtime readback pass. Preserve intended app guard; never deploy to legacy to bypass it.
